<reason>A more convincingly distinguished enforceable scrutiny from the motion’s specific standardization and publication requirements. It answered both pressure questions with a coherent alternative that supplies regulators and deployers actionable information, undercutting B’s repeated secrecy-versus-sunlight framing. B retained a meaningful case for broader public scrutiny and comparable information, but overstated both the alternative’s similarity to the motion and the verification possible from redacted summaries. A’s crowd-out argument remained speculative, and imperfect evaluations can still help, so this was a clear but competitive win rather than a decisive rejection of publication’s value.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B argued that researchers could check published aggregate safety results through API access. A correctly distinguished discovering failures from auditing an aggregate rate: without the underlying task distribution, discrepancies do not reliably establish gaming. This materially weakened B’s central verification claim without requiring A to deny that public reports can be useful.</best_rebuttal>
